guard: a CPN laptop session is fed its credential from an in-memory cell that IS the endpoint's creds source, adopts a same-nkey re-signed credential through the endpoint's prove-then-adopt transaction, swaps its live wire onto it, and — when either stage fails — leaves the cell and the endpoint's committed credential naming the SAME credential
why: The shipped defect: packages/core/src/endpoint.ts carries a complete prove-then-adopt renewal
system (fetch -> nkey pin -> preflight on a disposable connection -> commit -> re-arm) that is
armed by exactly one thing, `creds` being a FUNCTION. Every connector passed a STRING, so
`credsSource` was undefined and the whole apparatus was dead code on the laptop path: a CPN
session simply lost its mesh connection at its JWT's `exp`. M1 is that defect verbatim - the
endpoint handed a static string again - and it must redden the cell that asks the endpoint to
reload, not merely make some later check flaky.
The rollback is the other half, and it is the half with no obvious failure signal. By the time
`reloadCreds` RETURNS, the endpoint has already committed the candidate to `currentCreds` and
re-armed its 75% timer on the candidate's `exp` - and the wire presents `currentCreds`, not the
source. So a rollback that reverts only the CELL leaves the endpoint presenting the new
credential while the source returns the old one, and the next timer tick reads a credential
whose renewal delay is already negative, floors at 1s and spins until expiry. A rollback that
re-proves only the ENDPOINT leaves the cell behind the wire. Both are silent, both survive every
check that only asks whether an adoption succeeded, and M5 and M6 are the two of them: they
mutate opposite halves of the same catch block and must redden the SAME cell, which is why that
cell asserts the endpoint's window and the cell's window in one breath.

mutations.name: M1 the shipped defect: the endpoint gets a static string again
mutations.expectRed: the endpoint was built on a creds SOURCE, not a static string

mutations.name: M2 the cell's nkey pin is dropped
mutations.expectRed: a credential naming a DIFFERENT nkey is refused by the cell before anything moves

mutations.name: M3 adoption never swaps the wire
mutations.find:
// failure into { ok: false } (agent.ts:307-309) and would hide it from the rollback below.
      await this.ep.reconnect();
mutations.replace: // failure into { ok: false } (agent.ts:307-309) and would hide it from the rollback below.
mutations.expectRed: adoption swaps the LIVE connection within 20 seconds

mutations.name: M4 a refused candidate is left in the cell
mutations.find:
// adopted and reverting the cell alone is sufficient HERE and only here.
      cell.adopt(previous);
mutations.replace: // adopted and reverting the cell alone is sufficient HERE and only here.
mutations.expectRed: a credential the broker refuses leaves the session on the previous credential

mutations.name: M5 the reconnect rollback reverts the cell but not the endpoint
mutations.find: try { restored = await this.ep.reloadCreds(); } catch (e2) { restoreFailed = e2 as Error; }
mutations.expectRed: a failed wire swap puts BOTH the cell and the endpoint back on the previous credential

mutations.name: M6 the reconnect rollback reverts the endpoint but not the cell
mutations.expectRed: a failed wire swap puts BOTH the cell and the endpoint back on the previous credential

mutations.name: M7 overlapping adoptions are serialized
mutations.expectRed: the first refused reconnect cannot roll back over the second committed adoption
